triage.note: D10 defect 1 and the highest-leverage one: the postmortem calls a parameterised start URL the single change that bypasses S1 (fetch-then-render), S3 (three identical Extract buttons) and S4 (nothing waits for the async result) at once, because the agent lands on a page that is already rendered. There was no deep link at all. Pinned as WHOLE expressions for WIRE_UI's stated reason — a question about a hop ("does it read the query string?") is answerable by a broken hop. The pins carry the safe-degrade contract, which is the part most likely to rot: the membership guard returns before anything is assigned, so an absent or unknown `fixture` is a no-op and `run=1` alone extracts nothing. Client-side only: no server route changed, `/` still serves the same static file (display layer). WHERE THE CALL SITE SITS took three rounds to pin honestly, and the first pin of it is now the first entry of `wire`: one contiguous span from the options assignment, through the `catch` arm, to `deepLink();`. The call must be on `boot()`'s straight-line tail after `#fx` is filled from `/api/meta`, because the option list is exactly what the membership guard tests against. PR #55 R1 pinned guard-before-run, which is inert (that order is fixed by the function's own text). PR #55 R9 then measured both failure directions of the replacement, a position-comparing `order` chain, and both are re-measured here against the containment pin. FALSE GREEN then, RED now — `deepLink();` moved into the catch arm, where it runs only when /api/meta fails: `missing pinned expression (the deep link's wire): $("#fx").innerHTML = m.fixtures.map(f => `<option>${esc(f)}</option>`).join(""); }catch(e){ $("#sha").textContent = "meta unavailable"; } deepLink();`. FALSE RED then, GREEN now — the whole `function deepLink(){…}` declaration hoisted above `boot()`, which is behaviour-identical because declarations hoist: `[PASS] ui-deep-link`, invariant 63/63 = 1.000. Round 1's own mutation, `deepLink();` moved to the first line of `boot()`, stays red with the same missing-pin message. Re-measured against the pre-D10 file (3cdfbf4) the whole case is red at all six pins missing, six failures — the first being the span above and the rest `const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);`, `const want = q.get("fixture");`, `if(!want || ![...$("#fx").options].some(o => o.value === want)) return;`, `$("#fx").value = want;`, `if(q.get("run") === "1") $("#go-fx").click();`. No offsets are quoted anywhere in this note: the check emits none, and PR #55 R10 was raised because an earlier revision of this note quoted a pair the check could never have produced.
